cards.text: David's son Amnon violated his sister Tamar (2 Samuel 13:14). Her brother Absalom, another of David's sons, never said a word to Amnon after that, good or bad, because he hated him (2 Samuel 13:22). Two years later, Absalom's sheepshearers are at Baal-hazor near Ephraim.

cards.question: Absalom sends out invitations to his sheepshearing at Baal-hazor. Who does he invite?

answers.text: All the sons of the king

cards.question: Then Absalom goes to the king himself. No messenger, no note, the man shows up in PERSON. True or false: Absalom invites the king but asks him to leave his servants at home.
David tells Absalom they should not all go to the sheepshearing. What reason does David give?

answers.text: They would be a burden to Absalom
The road to Baal-hazor is too long
He has business at the palace

cards.text: Absalom urges him, but David still won't go and gives him his blessing instead. That's the royal version of RSVPing no with a big heart emoji.

cards.question: If the king won't come, Absalom asks that his brother ___ go with them.
David answers Absalom's request for Amnon with a question of his own. What does David ask?

answers.text: Why should he go with you

cards.text: Absalom urges him AGAIN, and the king sends Amnon and the rest of his sons. Friend, that man asks like an oven timer that won't quit beeping until somebody gets up.
But here's what the guest list doesn't show. Absalom has already given his young men orders about Amnon.

cards.question: Absalom tells his young men to watch Amnon and wait before they strike. What are they waiting for?

answers.text: Until Amnon's heart is merry with wine
Until Amnon falls asleep in his tent
Until the last sheep has been sheared

cards.question: Absalom's young men are being told to strike down a son of the king. True or false: Absalom tells them not to be afraid.

cards.text: And then it happens, friend. Absalom's young men do to Amnon just as Absalom ordered, and they kill him.

cards.question: Amnon is dead. What do the rest of the king's sons do?

answers.text: Each one flees on his mule

cards.text: The king's sons are still on the road. But news moves faster than a mule, and a report reaches David first.

cards.question: While the king's sons are still on the way, what does the report tell David?

answers.text: Absalom has struck down all the king's sons
Amnon has struck down his brother Absalom
Robbers have attacked the king's sons

cards.question: True or false: when David hears the report, he tears his clothes.

cards.text: Then David lies down on the ground, and all his servants stand by with their clothes torn.
Then Jonadab speaks up. He's the son of David's brother Shimeah, the same shrewd friend who told Amnon how to get Tamar to come to him (2 Samuel 13:3-5).

cards.question: The king is lying on the ground with his clothes torn. What does Jonadab tell him?
Jonadab tells David that Absalom planned this. Since when?

answers.text: Since the day Amnon violated Tamar
Since the day the shearers were hired
Since the day David blessed him

cards.text: Then Jonadab says it again: “Only Amnon is dead.” He tells the king not to take the report to heart.
Meanwhile, Absalom has fled. The young man standing watch looks up and sees many people coming down the road west of him, along the side of the hill.

cards.question: The watchman reports men coming from the direction of Horonaim. True or false: Jonadab tells the king the men coming are Absalom's young men.
True or false: as Jonadab finishes speaking, the king's sons come in wailing loudly.

cards.text: The king and all his servants weep very bitterly too. And Absalom flees to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur.

cards.question: Absalom is gone to Geshur, and every day David ___ for his son.
Absalom has fled to Geshur. How long does he stay there?

cards.text: And David's heart? It has been consoled over Amnon's death.

cards.question: Now that he's been consoled over Amnon's death, true or false: King David longs to go to Absalom.

cards.text: I'm stopping us right here, friend. This family's story isn't over. Not even close.
